title: Day-trader mode: genericize Triple Screen (Tide/Wave/Trigger) evaluation over the active timeframe triple
description:
Third of four dependent follow-up tasks splitting docs/tasks/backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode.json's original checklist items 5 and 9 out of that task (see its `decisions` entry for the full split rationale and what already landed: `app.signals.timeframe`'s generic TimeframeTriple model + `app.trading_mode`'s global settings persistence + `GET`/`PUT /api/settings/trading-mode`; and backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-ibkr-intraday's real intraday data fetching, a hard prerequisite here since there's no meaningful way to test a generic evaluation against day-trader-mode data without it).

This is the core methodology change: `app.signals.triple_screen.evaluate_tide`/`evaluate_wave`/`evaluate_trigger` and `app.signals.engine.analyse`/`analyse_history` currently hard-code weekly (Tide) / daily (Wave) / daily-as-Trigger-approximation (Screen 3) -- see `app.signals.engine._weekly_through_bar_date`'s calendar-week truncation logic and every 'weekly'/'daily'-named parameter throughout `engine.py`. This task adapts that evaluation to operate generically over whichever `TimeframeTriple` is currently active (`app.trading_mode.get_trading_mode_setting`) -- swing mode's own weekly/daily behavior must remain byte-for-byte unchanged (it's this app's default and only mode in production today; regression risk here is real, not hypothetical), while day-trader mode evaluates the same Screen 1/2/3 + Impulse + confidence logic over the configured triple's long-term/intermediate/short-term data instead.

Needs an `elder-signal-reviewer` pass before merge (docs/tasks/backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode.json's original checklist item 9) given ch. 39's own framing of what changes and what stays invariant when timeframes shift: confirm (don't assume) that the Impulse System, confidence scoring (docs/Analyse.md §6), and the 6% Rule/protective-stop risk logic (docs/Analyse.md §7) all remain timeframe-agnostic in principle once Screen 1/2/3 themselves are genericized. Also confirm docs/Analyse.md §7's own weekly-chart-specific profit-target/stop rule (ch. 39 p.161's 'set profit targets using long-term charts, stops on intermediate-timeframe charts') generalizes correctly to 'long-term chart' / 'intermediate-timeframe chart' meaning whichever timeframe currently fills that role, not literally weekly/daily -- this app's own `suggest_profit_target`/`protective_stop` currently hard-code that literal weekly/daily split (see docs/Analyse.md's 'Swing-style' profit-target section) and are explicitly out of scope for this task's own checklist unless the elder-signal-reviewer pass finds they must change too.

checklist.step: Decide (and record via `decisions`) how deep the genericization goes for this task's own scope: at minimum Screen 1/2/3 (`triple_screen.py`) + the Impulse gate's timeframe assumptions in `engine.py`; explicitly decide whether `portfolio/risk.py`/`portfolio/profit_target.py`'s hard-coded weekly/daily split is in scope here or deferred to yet another follow-up.

Genericize `app.signals.triple_screen.evaluate_tide`/`evaluate_wave`/`evaluate_trigger` to accept whichever long-term/intermediate/short-term data the active `TimeframeTriple` implies, with swing mode's existing weekly/daily behavior preserved exactly (regression tests, not just new-behavior tests).
Genericize `app.signals.engine.analyse`/`analyse_history`'s weekly/daily-specific truncation and parameter naming (`_weekly_through_bar_date` and friends) the same way.
Unit/integration tests for the generic evaluation, including a mocked IBKR intraday provider (no test may make a live network call) exercising an actual day-trader-mode signal computation end to end.
elder-signal-reviewer pass before merge -- confirm Impulse/confidence/6%-Rule timeframe-agnosticism per this task's own description, don't assume it.
Update docs/architecture/Backend.md §11's 'Not yet landed' list accordingly.

decisions.decision: Scope for this task's own PR: genericize `app.signals.triple_screen` (Tide/Wave/Trigger) and `app.signals.engine` (`analyse`/`analyse_history`'s orchestration, plus a new `analyse_day_trader` entry point). `app.portfolio.risk`/`app.portfolio.profit_target`/`app.portfolio.exits`'s own hard-coded weekly/daily split (the 6% Rule/protective-stop's `_SWING_LOW_WINDOW_DAYS` trading-day window, the weekly-chart profit-target channel, `evaluate_exit_flags`'s `tide_flipped_bearish` flag on `weekly_ohlcv`) is deferred to a follow-up task, not touched here. `app.data.day_trader_intraday` (a sibling, already-`done` task's module) is extended in this PR to also fetch the `long_term` leg, resolving a non-blocking finding from that task's own PR #311 review.
decisions.rationale: The task's own checklist explicitly permits deferring the portfolio/risk-layer split, and the actual code shows why that's the right call here specifically: `app.portfolio.risk.protective_stop`'s SafeZone-style swing-low window and `app.portfolio.profit_target.suggest_profit_target`'s weekly-chart channel are genuinely calendar-day/calendar-week-specific concepts (a '~2 weeks' lookback, a literal weekly-resampled OHLCV fetch) that would need their own dedicated design decisions (what does a '10 trading day' SafeZone window mean when the active short-term leg is 2-minute bars?) rather than a mechanical rename -- exactly the kind of judgment call that deserves its own task and its own elder-signal-reviewer scrutiny, not a rushed addendum to an already-large signal-engine change. Extending `app.data.day_trader_intraday` to fetch `long_term` was judged in-scope (not deferred) because `backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-ibkr-intraday-followups.json`'s own checklist explicitly named this task as the one that should decide it, and because ch. 39's own canonical day-trading examples (25-min/5-min/2-min, 39-min/8-min) are fully intraday on all three legs -- without this extension, this task's own end-to-end test (checklist item 4) couldn't exercise Screen 1/Tide against real day-trader-mode data for the book's own primary examples at all, which would have made 'genericize the evaluation' an unverifiable claim for the case that matters most.

decisions.decision: `app.signals.engine.analyse`'s existing public parameters (`daily_ohlcv`, `weekly_ohlcv`) and `app.signals.triple_screen.evaluate_tide`/`evaluate_wave`'s existing parameters are NOT renamed to generic names -- genericity is achieved by documenting the general contract (a short added docstring paragraph on each) and, for `analyse()`, by adding a new optional `short_term_ohlcv` parameter, rather than by renaming what's already there. `evaluate_trigger`'s own `daily_ohlcv` parameter IS renamed, to `ohlcv`. The private, zero-external-caller `_weekly_through_bar_date` helper and `_WAVE_LOOKBACK_DAYS` constant in `engine.py` ARE renamed (`_long_term_through_bar_date`/`_WAVE_LOOKBACK_BARS`), since checklist item 3 explicitly names the former by example.
decisions.rationale: `evaluate_tide`/`evaluate_wave`/`analyse()`'s `daily_ohlcv`/`weekly_ohlcv` parameters already accept an arbitrary `pd.DataFrame` -- nothing in their implementation is actually specific to calendar weeks/days, only the parameter *names* and the surrounding prose are. Renaming them would touch roughly 150 occurrences of those identifiers across `engine.py`/`triple_screen.py`'s own extremely dense narrative docstrings (confirmed via grep before starting), for zero behavioral difference, at real risk of introducing a subtle prose error mid-edit that a passing test suite would never catch (a wrong word in a docstring doesn't fail an assertion) -- directly working against this task's own explicit 'be extremely careful, given real regression risk on swing mode' instruction, since verifying a rename of that size by eye is itself expensive and error-prone. `evaluate_trigger` is the deliberate exception: unlike Tide/Wave, its own *meaning* genuinely changes depending on what's fed in (swing mode's daily-bar EOD approximation vs. day-trader mode's literal short-term-timeframe rule) -- see its own rewritten docstring -- so renaming its parameter to a neutral `ohlcv` and rewriting that one function's (much shorter, ~35-line) docstring to explain both cases was worth the smaller, more contained risk. Confirmed via `grep` before renaming that every real caller of `evaluate_trigger`/`analyse`/`analyse_history` in `app/` and `tests/` uses positional arguments only (no `daily_ohlcv=`/`weekly_ohlcv=` keyword usage anywhere), so even the parameters that keep their old names would have tolerated a rename without breaking a caller -- the decision not to rename them is about diff-size/review-risk, not caller compatibility.

decisions.decision: `app.signals.engine.analyse`'s Screen 3 (Trigger) genericization is a new optional `short_term_ohlcv: pd.DataFrame | None = None` parameter -- when `None` (the default, every existing caller's behavior), Trigger evaluates on `daily_ohlcv` exactly as before; when supplied, Trigger evaluates on `short_term_ohlcv` instead, while Screen 1 (Tide)/Screen 2 (Wave)/the Impulse gate/every `indicators` entry are completely unaffected (still read `daily_ohlcv`/`weekly_ohlcv`). A new `analyse_day_trader()` function is the day-trader-mode entry point -- a thin wrapper supplying `long_term_ohlcv`/`intermediate_ohlcv`/`short_term_ohlcv` explicitly and delegating straight to `analyse()`, with no DB/IBKR dependency of its own.
decisions.rationale: This maps directly onto ch. 39's own three-tier structure: Tide is the long-term screen, Wave is the medium-term/intermediate screen, and Trigger is specifically the short-term/intraday screen (docs/Analyse.md §2's own 'Screen 3 -- The Ripple (entry trigger, short-term/intraday)' heading) -- so Trigger is the *only* one of the three that should ever read a genuinely distinct short-term series in day-trader mode; Wave/the Impulse gate/every daily indicator correctly stay on whichever data plays the intermediate role (verified directly: `evaluate_impulse`'s own docstring already documents its `ohlcv` parameter as timeframe-agnostic, confirming the Impulse gate needed no change at all here). A default of `None` reproducing the exact pre-existing call path was chosen specifically so swing mode's own regression tests (unchanged assertions, still passing) constitute genuine proof of no behavior change, rather than requiring a new code path to be proven equivalent to an old one that no longer exists. `analyse_day_trader()` staying a pure function (no DB Session/IBKR provider parameter) keeps `app.signals.engine` a DB- and IBKR-free domain module, matching docs/architecture/Backend.md §5's existing description of this module -- resolving *which* frames to fetch for the currently active `TimeframeTriple` is left to `backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-api` (a dependent follow-up task, not yet started), which is where DB/IBKR wiring for an actual HTTP route belongs.

decisions.decision: `analyse_history()`'s own day-trader-mode support (a walk-forward historical replay producing a per-bar signal history over intraday data, for a future day-trader-mode chart overlay) is deferred to a follow-up task, not built here. `_long_term_through_bar_date` (renamed from `_weekly_through_bar_date`) does gain a `long_term_unit: TimeframeUnit = TimeframeUnit.WEEK` parameter with a new direct `<= bar_date` branch for `DAY`/`MINUTE` units (covered by dedicated unit tests), but `analyse_history()`'s own public signature is unchanged and its one internal call site still passes the default `WEEK` unit -- exactly its pre-existing behavior.
decisions.rationale: `app.data.day_trader_intraday`'s current shape (`get_intraday_bars_for_triple`/`get_active_day_trader_intraday_bars`) only ever fetches 'the most recent N days of bars, as of now' -- a signal-computation snapshot, the right shape for `analyse()`/`analyse_day_trader()`'s single-point-in-time evaluation (this task's checklist item 4's own 'actual day-trader-mode signal computation' framing, singular). Walking forward through *historical* intraday bars for a growing per-bar replay (what `analyse_history` does for swing mode) needs a categorically different IBKR fetch shape -- paginating backward through a much longer intraday history window while still respecting IBKR's per-call pagination bounds (`IBKRProvider._MAX_PAGINATION_PAGES`/`_MAX_BARS_PER_PAGE`) -- that's a genuine, unsolved data-fetching design problem in its own right, not a mechanical extension of this task's own engine-layer changes. Building `_long_term_through_bar_date`'s `DAY`/`MINUTE` branch now (rather than waiting for that follow-up) was still worth doing: it's cheap, correct, and directly testable in isolation (see `TestLongTermThroughBarDateGenericUnits`), so the follow-up task inherits a ready building block instead of needing to touch this function's own look-ahead-avoidance logic itself.

comments.summary: Non-blocking: `app.signals.confidence.score_volume_confirmation`'s "trigger bar volume" arm reads `daily_ohlcv["volume"]` (the intermediate leg) unconditionally in `analyse()`, even when `short_term_ohlcv` is supplied and Trigger fires against a genuinely distinct short-term series -- so in day-trader mode the volume-confirmation component checks the intermediate bar's volume, not the actual triggering short-term bar's volume, a real (narrow, OR'd-with-Force-Index-spike) drift from docs/Analyse.md §6's "trigger bar volume" language once Screen 3 no longer shares Wave's timeframe. No live impact today since nothing in app/api/routers or app/portfolio references TradingMode/analyse_day_trader yet, but the PR's own self-review overstates full confidence-scoring timeframe-agnosticism on this one point. Tracked as backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-signal-engine-followups.

Non-blocking: `TimeframeUnit`'s class docstring still references `app.signals.engine._weekly_through_bar_date`, which this PR itself renamed to `_long_term_through_bar_date` -- a stale identifier left behind by the rename (every other reference in docs/architecture/Backend.md and engine.py/tests was updated correctly). Tracked as backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-signal-engine-followups.

Non-blocking/bookkeeping: this PR resolves backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-ibkr-intraday-followups.json's checklist item 3 (fetching the long_term leg for a fully-intraday triple) in substance, but that followup task's own checklist entry was never marked done to reflect it. Tracked as backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-signal-engine-followups.

Non-blocking: `get_intraday_bars_for_triple` now issues three sequential synchronous IBKR round-trips (extended from two by this PR) instead of fetching the independent per-leg data concurrently -- for a fully-intraday triple this now costs 3x sequential latency instead of 2x. The same concern is already tracked (for the two-leg case) on backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-ibkr-intraday-followups.json's checklist item 1; also confirmed independently by a code-review (effort: high) pass over this diff. Tracked as backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-signal-engine-followups.

review.notes: Full review of PR #312 (task/backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-signal-engine). Tests: backend 1319 passed, 100% line/branch coverage; frontend 882 passed, 99.77%/99.08%/99.79%/99.82% stmt/branch/func/line coverage -- both well above the 90% gate, no regression. Static analysis: ruff, mypy, eslint, tsc -b --noEmit, and scripts/check_profit_target_wording.py all clean. backend/openapi.json re-generated locally and diffed byte-identical against the committed snapshot (the only backend/API-facing change in this PR is a docstring comment in stocks.py, correctly mirrored into openapi.json/types.ts). Swing-mode byte-identical regression independently re-verified (not just trusting the PR's own claim): wrote a standalone script computing analyse()/analyse_history() over 4 independent scenarios (a 300-bar random walk, a 200-bar bullish trend, a 5-bar short-history edge case, and a 100-bar analyse_history walk-forward range) once on main (via a throwaway git worktree) and once on this branch, dumping every field (signal/confidence/confidence_band/breakdown/screens/indicators/divergence/kangaroo_tail) to JSON and diffing -- zero differences. elder-signal-reviewer pass (verify-elder-signal skill, applied rigorously): Screen 1/Tide is still exactly the weekly-Impulse-color methodology correction (unchanged, confirmed via evaluate_tide's own code, not just its docstring); the Impulse gate's two-independent-timeframe decoupling (weekly Tide-driving color vs. daily entry-gate color, both via the same evaluate_impulse call) is intact; _determine_signal's BUY/SELL/HOLD gating logic is byte-for-byte unchanged; confidence weights (30/20/25/15/10) and every component's derivation are unchanged except the volume-confirmation gap noted above. Confirmed the portfolio/risk.py deferral creates no live inconsistency today: grepped app/api/routers and app/portfolio for TradingMode/analyse_day_trader references and found none -- day-trader mode has zero wiring anywhere in the API/portfolio layer yet, so nothing can silently combine a day-trader-mode signal with swing-mode-only risk/profit-target math through any real endpoint; the deferral to backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-portfolio-risk (created by this PR) is a sound scope call, not a half-working state. Read the new integration test (tests/integration/test_day_trader_mode_signal_engine.py) critically: it exercises trading_mode settings -> mocked-IBKR intraday fetching (all 3 legs, matching ch. 39's fully-intraday canonical examples) -> analyse_day_trader end to end, genuinely proves the short-term leg (not the intermediate leg) drives the Trigger result via a fixture where only the 2-minute short_term series can fire the trigger, and asserts a real BUY with a valid confidence/breakdown shape -- sound, not just a green check. Reviewed the two new follow-up tasks this PR created (backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-portfolio-risk, backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-history): both well-scoped, correctly reference this task and each other's dependencies, and correctly frame the genuine open design questions (bar-count-window generalization, weekly-chart profit-target scope decision, IBKR historical-fetch pagination design) rather than presenting them as solved. Decision-memory cross-check: the one 'decide X' checklist item (checklist item 1, genericization scope) has a full decisions entry with rationale; the other three decisions entries (parameter-rename scope, short_term_ohlcv wiring, analyse_history deferral) are also properly recorded, not left implicit in code. No new module/dependency/layer added (only existing modules extended), so architecture-review was not run -- not applicable. No UI-facing work: this PR touches only backend/app/signals, backend/app/data/day_trader_intraday.py, and docs -- no API route, schema, or frontend component changed (the one frontend/backend touch is a byte-for-byte docstring-comment mirror in openapi.json/types.ts) -- so the browser walkthrough (step 9) and the persisted e2e suite (step 9a) were both explicitly skipped as not applicable, not silently omitted. git worktree used for the main-branch regression comparison was removed after use; the pre-existing 'not mine, do not discard' stash entry was left completely untouched throughout (git stash was never invoked). Also ran a full code-review (skill, effort high) pass over the diff as a corroborating check: it independently traced every renamed symbol to all call sites, verified the analyse_day_trader/short_term_ohlcv wiring and the DayTraderIntradayBars long_term extension against every constructor/call site, found no correctness bugs, and independently surfaced the same stale timeframe.py docstring reference plus the sequential-IBKR-fetch-latency point noted above. Four non-blocking findings total recorded above and filed as backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-signal-engine-followups (checklist items, not yet done).
